h1: CDL & Commercial Driver Ticket Lawyer in El Paso, Texas
intro: A traffic ticket is a nuisance for most drivers. For a CDL holder it is a threat to your livelihood, because the easy outs — deferred disposition and defensive driving — are not available to you. For a flat fee from $59, attorney Robert Navar fights for the dismissal that keeps your record clean.
summary: Federal rules generally prohibit Texas courts from "masking" a CDL holder's conviction — no deferred disposition, no defensive driving dismissal — so a CDL ticket is either fought for dismissal or it becomes a conviction on your record.
This applies even in your personal car: a speeding ticket in your pickup on the weekend counts against your CDL just like one in the truck.

Two "serious" violations (15+ mph over, following too closely, improper lane change, texting, and others) within three years bring a 60-day CDL disqualification; a third brings 120 days. Employers and DAC reports see every conviction.
We handle CDL tickets in El Paso Municipal Court ($59) and the JP, Horizon City, Socorro, San Elizario, Clint and Anthony courts ($69). Hire online in two minutes.

sections.heading: Why a CDL Ticket Is Different From Everyone Else's
paragraphs: When a regular driver gets a speeding ticket in El Paso, the court will usually offer deferred disposition or a defensive driving course, and the ticket disappears without a conviction. Texas law itself excludes CDL holders from the driving safety course dismissal (Code of Criminal Procedure art. 45.0511), and federal regulations go further: under the FMCSA's anti-masking rule (49 CFR 384.226, stated generally) a state may not defer, divert or otherwise keep a CDL holder's traffic conviction off the record. Texas enforces this in every municipal and JP court.

The practical result is binary. Either the ticket is dismissed on its merits or by negotiation, or you plead and it goes to DPS and into your federal CDLIS record. There is no middle option, which is why CDL drivers who "just pay it" to save time are making the most expensive choice available.

Our office has fought commercial driver tickets in El Paso for more than a decade. We know which prosecutors will reduce a charge to a non-moving violation, which judges want a clean motor vehicle record before they'll dismiss, and how to build the file so dismissal is the easiest answer for the court. This page is general information, not legal advice about your case.

sections.heading: Serious Violations and the 60/120-Day Disqualification
paragraphs: The federal CDL rules sort violations into tiers. Routine convictions — a few miles over the limit, an equipment ticket — add up on your DPS record and with your insurer but don't by themselves disqualify you. "Serious traffic violations" are different. Two of them in any commercial motor vehicle within three years bring a 60-day disqualification of your CDL; three within three years bring 120 days. No work, no paycheck, and a mark your carrier's safety department will see.

sections.heading: Tickets in Your Personal Vehicle Still Count
paragraphs: The question we get most from CDL drivers is whether the Saturday speeding ticket in the family SUV matters. It does. Texas reports every conviction to DPS, and your license is a commercial license whether or not you were working at the time. A serious violation in a personal vehicle can also count toward the two-in-three-years disqualification rule — and either way it lands on the motor vehicle record your employer pulls each year.

Your employer sees more than the MVR. Carriers that subscribe to the DAC employment history report and FMCSA's Pre-Employment Screening Program see violations and inspection results, and some carriers terminate drivers after a set number of convictions regardless of circumstances. We have had clients call because dispatch told them one conviction would end their contract. The time to call is before the appearance date, not after.
If you also hold a hazmat endorsement or drive for a company with a tight safety rating, mention it when you hire us — it changes how aggressively we push for a dismissal versus a reduced charge.

sections.heading: How Robert Navar Fights CDL Tickets in El Paso Courts
paragraphs: When you hire us online or call 915-503-1600, we file a notice of appearance the same business day. That stops any failure-to-appear warrant and routes everything to our office — important for drivers who are on the road in another state when the court date arrives.

Then we build the case. We pull the citation and the officer's notes; for speeding, the radar or lidar calibration records; for lane-change and following-too-close tickets, the dash camera and any crash report. Many CDL tickets have fixable problems — a wrong statute, an officer who has left the department, a speed measured on a grade where the device's tolerance matters. We present that to the prosecutor on the pretrial docket and negotiate for an outright dismissal. Where a dismissal isn't available, we work for a reduction to a non-moving violation such as defective equipment, which is reported differently and is not a serious violation under the federal rules.

Tickets from El Paso Police go to El Paso Municipal Court; tickets from a DPS trooper or deputy on I-10 go to a Justice of the Peace precinct; Anthony and Vinton write a steady stream of truck tickets on the west side. Each court has its own prosecutor and habits, and we appear in all of them.

sections.heading: Ports of Entry, the Zaragoza Bridge and Cross-Border Drivers
paragraphs: El Paso's trucking traffic is unlike any other Texas city's. Thousands of commercial vehicles cross daily at the Ysleta–Zaragoza port of entry and move along Zaragoza Road, Joe Battle Boulevard and the Border Highway to warehouses and transload yards. Police, DPS and the Sheriff all work those corridors, and a driver pulling a drayage load from Juárez to an east-side yard can collect a citation in the two miles between the bridge and the dock.

Many of those drivers hold Mexican commercial licenses (Licencia Federal) rather than a Texas CDL, which raises its own questions about how a Texas conviction is reported and whether carrier status is affected. We handle those cases regularly. Se habla español. If you are dealing with a roadside inspection, overweight or logbook citation rather than a moving violation, see our trucking and DOT violations page — those tickets have a different structure and usually land in JP court. Not sure which court has your citation? Use the free ticket and warrant lookup.

faqs.q: Can a CDL holder take defensive driving to dismiss a ticket in Texas?
faqs.a: No. Texas excludes CDL holders from the driving safety course dismissal, and federal anti-masking rules generally prohibit the court from using deferred disposition or any other program to keep a CDL holder's conviction off the record. The ticket has to be dismissed or reduced on the merits, which is what we do.

faqs.q: Does a ticket in my personal vehicle affect my CDL?
faqs.a: Yes. Convictions in a personal vehicle are reported on your commercial license and show up on the motor vehicle record your employer pulls. Serious violations in a personal vehicle can also count toward a CDL disqualification.

faqs.q: What is a "serious traffic violation" for CDL purposes?
faqs.a: Under federal rules, these include speeding 15 mph or more over the limit, following too closely, improper lane changes, reckless driving, texting or hand-held phone use, and driving a commercial vehicle without a CDL or the proper endorsement. Two convictions in three years bring a 60-day disqualification; three bring 120 days.

faqs.q: Will my employer find out about the ticket?
faqs.a: If it becomes a conviction, almost certainly. Carriers pull motor vehicle records at least annually and many subscribe to DAC and PSP reports. A dismissed ticket does not appear as a conviction, which is why fighting the ticket is the only real way to keep it from your employer.

faqs.q: I'm on the road out of state. Do I have to come back for court?
faqs.a: For most Class C tickets in El Paso County, no. We file an appearance and handle the pretrial docket for you. The only time you would need to be present is a trial, which is rare and something we'd plan with you around your schedule.

faqs.a: The same flat fee as any ticket: $59 in El Paso Municipal Court and $69 in JP, Horizon City, Socorro, San Elizario, Clint and Anthony courts. Multiple citations from the same stop are discounted add-ons. Given what a conviction costs a commercial driver, it is the best money you'll spend this year.
